mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month indicates a weakening demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST decreased by more than 5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month signals labor market stress, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.3pp within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal: a high level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS/GDPC1 is high.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal: when industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% in a month and CPI (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 0.5% increase), it indicates a positive supply shock, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increase > 1% and CPIAUCSL increase < 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% and CPIAUCSL increased by less than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal: during periods of economic expansion (indicated by PAYEMS increasing by more than 1% in 3 months), a stable or decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tight labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 1% in 3 months and UNRATE stable or decreasing
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 1% in 3 months and UNRATE was stable or decreasing.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal: a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to historical averages indicates accommodative monetary policy, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is below its historical average.

mechanism_narrative: A threshold-triggered signal: a significant increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% in a quarter indicates strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% in a quarter.
